> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `504e4860f6827a090b1ccbcedbc12cbffaea0125` — the merge of head `f6a224d16daa1c9f5448edbee491053a73c7d1ec` into base `ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 504e4860f6827a090b1ccbcedbc12cbffaea0125 && git checkout 504e4860f6827a090b1ccbcedbc12cbffaea0125
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 f6a224d16daa1c9f5448edbee491053a73c7d1ec && git checkout -B drift-repro ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 && git merge --no-ff f6a224d16daa1c9f5448edbee491053a73c7d1ec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise re-derived, holds.** On `main` the gate resolves `allowed` with `resolveSearchFieldResolution` over the unfiltered `gate.fields`, so a declared `secret` / `password` entry stays in the allowed set and the request passes; the engine's `expandSearchOnAst` (engine.ts, the ADR-0100 block before `expandOptions`) builds `scanFields` minus `collectInternalReadFields ∪ collectCredentialFields`, so `resolveSearchFields` validates the requested credential to an empty list and, by its documented tolerance, returns the rest of the declared set — the card's "narrower asked, wider answered". The fix refuses the name at the door where the allowed set KEPT it; the engine is untouched as the floor.
- **Predicate parity (point 1): exact.** `isCredentialFieldType` (spec `masked-field-types.ts`) answers from the own keys of `MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES`, which are `secret` and `password`; `collectCredentialFields` (objectql `secret-fields.ts`) calls that same function per field, and so does the lint's credential check (`validate-searchable-fields.ts`). The `FieldType` enum (spec `field.zod.ts`) carries no other credential-like member — no token or encrypted type exists (the #13716 note in `search-fields.ts` records that `'encrypted'` never did). Both sides are exemption-free (a better-auth `password` is withheld and refused alike). No credential the engine withholds now passes the gate; nothing non-credential is newly refused. The flag-keyed half (`internal: true`) was already refused first (#22646) by the cross-package twin of the engine's reader.
- **Reach (point 2): one gate, no bypass found.** The call sits in `findData`'s normalizer (protocol.ts, the #4254 block): `options.searchFields` when present — the `$searchFields` alias is lowered to it above, string and array alike — else the object-form `search.fields`. Doors that pass a caller override through `findData`: `GET /data/:object` and `POST /data/:object/query` (crud-routes), the export route (`data-action-routes.ts` builds `searchFields` and hands it to `p.findData`); the other `findData` callers (import-runner, connector-pull, action-execution, admin-import-users) carry no search override. `GET /api/v1/search` (`searchAll`, `protocol-record-reads.ts`) sends a SERVER-derived list to `engine.find` — ADR-0061 Tier 1, the client sends only the term — so there is no caller narrowing to refuse there. `packages/mcp` carries no search override. Hooks and flows reach the engine directly, where the tolerant intersection is the documented posture for callers that pass no ingress. The count leg reuses the post-gate `options.searchFields`, so `total` and the page agree.
- **Cascade and envelope.** `credential` is a subset of `allowedSet`; `unknown`, `staleDeclared`, `virtual`, `unsearchable` are subsets of its complement — disjoint, so the order only chooses the leading message: typo-class answers first, credential before the generic `unsearchable`. The thrown error carries `code INVALID_FIELD`, `status 400`, `field`, `fields`, `object`, `param` — the tail every reason of this gate uses. The runtime string carries no tracker number.
- **Console producers (point 3): only a lint-errored declaration moves.** `ListView.tsx` (the `$searchFields` spread in the list fetch) and `objectGridRowLoad.ts` (the `params.$searchFields` assignment) send `schema.searchableFields` of the VIEW node; the fallbacks in `ObjectView.tsx` (`currentNamedViewConfig ?? activeView ?? schema`, where `schema` is `ObjectViewSchema`) and `objectViewListRenderer.tsx` (`viewDef ?? listSchema`) are view-level too. `objectResolvesSearch` in `ListView.tsx` reads the OBJECT's declaration only to decide whether to draw the box and sends nothing from it. Hard-coded sets in app-shell (`builtinComponents.tsx`, metadata-admin `anchors.ts`) name no credential. So the one producer that goes 200 → 400 is a view declaring a credential entry, which `validate-searchable-fields` already reports as `error` on every surface, object and view. The acceptance note holds; the dogfood battery at this head is green, and the one platform object I read with a long declared set (`sys_approval_request`) names no credential.
- **The test (point 5).** Real `RestServer` → `findData` → `ObjectQL` → `SqlDriver` (sqlite), both credential types, GET and POST, standalone and object-form slots, plus three controls per type. The refusal legs assert the NEW branch's own sentence (`Field 'api_key' on object '…' is type '…'`), which the auto-default's "is not searchable" wording cannot satisfy, so a regression to the old path fails on the message as well as the status. `engine.find` reaches `driver.find` (engine.ts, the hook-wrapped read), so the wrapped counter is live; the file does not pin a positive increment — same shape as its sibling `data-empty-search-fields-door.test.ts` (should-fix in ④). The ablation on record gated the one new cascade arm behind a global: four refusal legs answered 200, controls stayed green, HEAD blob restored, `--absent` preflight clean — it isolates the new arm as the carrier.
- **Dev report cross-checks.** `dogfood_battery` names `f6a224d1`, which is this head (merge of `origin/main` `d770b150` onto the fix `1d6b7d0d`). Deviation (2) verified: `git log 1d6b7d0d..f6a224d1 -- packages/rest/src` is empty, so the two merges brought no `rest` change; #27860 (`7591c603`) touched `protocol.ts` by 13 lines in the datasource credentials-ref block, not the search block, and the metadata-protocol suite was re-run at this head per the report. `open_questions: []`.
- **Check-runs on this head at 2026-10-30T04:50Z:** 32 success, 14 skipped, 6 in progress (Test Core 2/8–6/8, Type Check · workspace), 0 failed. Green already: Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Test Core 1/8, 7/8, 8/8, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, Docs drift flag. The running ones are the gate verdicts for what they cover; this record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **patch**, BREAKING banner, `!` title, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset, `Metadata-protocol: none` — right. What a metadata author can write is unchanged (the `searchableFields` schema still admits the entry; the lint already errors on it); the narrowing is on a QUERY value at the door. Post-Task #3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the documented category and fits: no key, export or type added, removed or re-shaped; the remedy is in the refusal. `Check Changeset` green.
- `@objectstack/rest`: only a test file, nothing publishes — correctly absent. `content/docs` and `.changeset` are not packages.
- `Skills-docs: none` verified by grep at this head: no skill names a credential beside `searchFields` / `searchableFields`.
- Tier: the file list carries no governed path and no published schema; the changeset's `(narrowing)` arm decides the face, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the tier owed and served.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Scope kept as the card asked: no `packages/spec/src/**` hunk, no engine hunk, no line of `protocol.ts`. The hot-file intersection the triage named (#27860) is merged into this head.
- Dev deviations, both acceptable: (1) a second `main` merge after four dogfood failures `main` fixed in #27878 / #27873 — the final battery is on the final head, which is what discipline §10 asks; (2) the full `rest` suite only on `1d6b7d0d` — verified no `rest` change arrived with the merges, and the CI Test Core shards cover it.
- Pre-existing, not this PR's defects; noted for the lane, no card filed by this review: (a) the `declared` branch's "not searchable" message lists `allowed.join(', ')`, which still names a declared credential (the dev's own note; should-fix in ④); (b) `searchAll` mirrors the internal-field withhold into its skip judgement but not the credential one, so a credential-only declaration is not skipped and reaches the engine, which falls to the auto default — the lint-errored degenerate case, unchanged here; (c) lint `rule-explanations.ts` `SEARCH_FIELDS_ECHO` says the ingress "refuses an entry outside the object's allowed set" — now also a declared credential inside it; `error-catalog.mdx` describes the `searchFields` reasons at a grain that names neither virtual nor credential, consistent with before. The docs-drift list was read; `data-api.mdx` is the one page that enumerates the refusals, and it gained its row.
- Who sees the 400: an API caller echoing an object's lint-errored declaration, and the Console on a view with such a declaration. This is the narrowing the triage ruled. Rollback is a revert.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts` — holds against the code it cites: one predicate shared by gate, engine and lint, no new type list; the refusal placed where #4254 put the loudness (the ingress) with the engine withhold untouched as the fail-closed floor; the branch fires only on the declared path by construction (the auto default never keeps a credential), and the comment says exactly that. The message names the type, says why the narrowing cannot be honoured, and names the declaration remedy (the `declaredSet.has(first)` guard is always true in this branch — harmless). The gate's own docblock in `protocol.ts` ("cannot admit a field the engine would then decline to scan") is now true on the credential axis where it was false. Must-fix: none. **Should-fix (non-blocking):** filter credential names out of the set the `declared` branch lists, with the same predicate, so the remedy text does not advertise a column the engine never scans.
- `packages/rest/src/data-search-fields-credential-door.test.ts` — right layer (the door over a real driver), both types, both verbs, both slots, controls, zero-read pin, and a message assertion that distinguishes the new arm from the auto-default refusal. **Should-fix (non-blocking):** pin that a control increments `reads.n` once, so the zero-read assertion is proven live rather than vacuously true; the sibling harness shares the gap.
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx` — the row fits the table's grammar, states the refusal and the remedy, and is accurate against the gate.
- `.changeset/27829-search-fields-credential-refused.md` — before / now / unchanged / who-sees-it / remedy, both declaration lines, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, BREAKING banner; the "who sees it" paragraph matches what the Console producers actually send.
